chain: (1) DATO: d-APV 50 uM eliminated the spontaneous bursts and the effect reversed (34634460 Results 2.2; 51 bursts, 5 slices, 3 animals; legend). -> (2) DATO: no AMPA/kainate antagonist was applied and the text has one AMPA word; AMPA dependence is untested within the perimeter of the paper text and supplement. -> (3) INFERENZA: the knockout mEPSC amplitude distribution is shifted to larger events at -70 mV with a decay of about 5 ms (5.18 vs 4.84 ms), the kinetic signature of an AMPA-type quantum; the pooled-event KS p values are inflated and are not used as confirmation, and the sEPSC mean differs by only about 6 percent. -> (4) IPOTESI: AMPAR current is a required step in burst initiation, with NMDAR current required for the burst as d-APV shows (burst-onset reversal about 6 mV is compatible with any glutamate cation channel). -> (5) IPOTESI, benefit: if bursts need AMPAR current, an AMPA-directed question (class transfer from the felbamate/perampanel nomination) becomes testable in this slice; if bursts survive a verified AMPA block, that question is dropped for this preparation
pharmacological_action: Block AMPA/kainate receptors to a verified extent and read whether bursts survive (new measurement, not a literature question)
compound_or_probe: Perampanel is the compound whose mechanism was read (25229608: noncompetitive negative allosteric AMPA/kainate antagonist; cultured rat hippocampal neurons, -60 mV, NMDA 10 and 100 uM currents unchanged by 30 uM; text and Table 1 IC50 0.4 to 1.2 uM; the Fig 1D curves read about 1 and 3-5 uM only if the printed axis numerals are used, and read by the tick marks they agree with the text (about 0.45 and 1 uM), so the earlier conflict is withdrawn as a probable axis-label misread, INFERENZA; slow onset and offset, off rate 0.58 per second). NBQX and GYKI 52466 are use-only or carried; no primary mechanism or selectivity paper for them was read (open routes absent). The decision rests on the measured fast-EPSC block, not on a tool
context: Neuron-specific Synapsin-Cre Wwox knockout, neocortical slices P13-P17, recording medium and Mg2+ measured (M01), 35 C as in the source; endpoints burst incidence, frequency, duration, burst-onset current, fast fEPSP and mEPSC for block verification; transfer from culture perampanel kinetics to the slice is unmeasured
competing_explanation: H2/H3: bursts are NMDAR-regenerative (AMPAR block may spare them or may abolish them through loss of the depolarisation that relieves the Mg2+ block, so abolition does not separate H1 from H2/H3); kainate-receptor contribution not separated (M17); H4: any large cut of excitation abolishes them (not receptor-specific); H7: dependence on the bath
counter_evidence: Perampanel did not alter NMDA currents in culture (supports NMDAR-sparing) but that is not a slice result; NBQX and perampanel were never applied to a Wwox system (F04 limits); heterozygote bursts show the phenotype is not confined to the knockout; a bursting slice in which AMPA block abolishes bursts does not show that AMPAR carries the defect (a drug response is not proof of a defect in its target)
weakening_result: Bursts persist at a verified fast-EPSC block at or above a threshold pre-specified before the experiment (about 90 percent is a design value with no source; the measured block is reported as a variable) (H1 weakened for this preparation); or bursts are abolished at the same percent of total evoked charge removed as d-APV needs (H4, no receptor specificity: M08)
discriminating_experiment: M01 then M02, M07 with verification, M08 (matched charge), M15 (genotype comparator); AMPA antagonist first, d-APV added only if bursts persist; washout order per M07
status: IPOTESI; exploratory; premise not established; independent audit: PARTLY (perampanel potency caveat withdrawn, H2 prediction under M07 corrected, kainate not separated). What it now rests on: the absence of any AMPA/kainate test in the paper, the survival-under-verified-block kill condition, and a new measurement
what_would_change_the_decision: A verified-complete AMPA block that spares bursts removes the AMPA arm; a block that abolishes bursts at less total charge removed than d-APV needs puts AMPAR first in the next pharmacological question. Neither can be replaced by literature on other epilepsy models, and NBQX or GYKI use needs a mechanism paper that was not reached. NEW MEASUREMENTS (not literature): within-slice paired design (each slice its own baseline, replacing the pooled-baseline unpaired comparisons of the source); recording Mg2+ and K+ as measured bath values; a receptor-agnostic release-reducing control; a floor control for the delayed-response metric.

chain: (1) DATO: bursts need NMDAR activity at the d-APV concentration used (OB04); the delayed evoked response is larger in the knockout (about 0.46 vs about 0.12 mV at 100 uA, INFERENZA from the figure) and is reduced by d-APV to about 0.4 of baseline at 100 uA and overshoots on washout (about 1.3), but the amplitude metric has a floor (wild type reads about 0.115 mV), so against the floor about 20 percent of the delayed component remains (INFERENZA); the residual is not used as evidence of incomplete block (Fig S3; OB08, OB09). -> (2) DATO: no isolated NMDAR current, subunit, glycine or Mg2+ datum exists for this preparation; recording Mg2+ not stated; resting potential is 5.6 mV more depolarised (Table 1). -> (3) INFERENZA: NMDAR dependence of the burst can arise from NMDAR gain, from permissive necessity in a depolarised, less inhibited network, or from AMPAR-led drive; these are not separated (module card F04). -> (4) IPOTESI: a GluN2B-containing component sustains the burst beyond what total NMDAR current predicts (curve left of matched d-APV). -> (5) IPOTESI, benefit: a pharmacological question can then be posed at the receptor-composition level instead of 'any antagonist'; coincident curves instead say the question is about total gain
pharmacological_action: Reduce NMDAR current by a measured fraction with a subunit-preferring modulator and compare with total block (d-APV) at matched fractions
compound_or_probe: Radiprodil (40994429, oocytes at room temperature with 100 uM glutamate and 30 uM glycine: IC50 0.029 uM at human GluN1-1a/GluN2B; no effect on GluN2A, GluN2C or GluN2D diheteromers; GluN2A/GluN2B triheteromers 45 percent maximum inhibition; 4.7 percent recovery after 3 min washout; mouse CA1 slices P17-P22, +40 mV, NBQX and gabazine, 3 uM reduced the evoked NMDAR EPSC) as the NAM whose mechanism was read; use or activity dependence untested. TCN-201 (22553026: recombinant GluN1/GluN2A, more than 1000-fold selective at 3 uM glycine, IC50 100 nM at 1 uM and 1.6 uM at 30 uM glycine, none at 300 uM, solubility 18 uM) only with a measured slice co-agonist level. The activity-dependence abstracts for ifenprodil and Ro 25-6981 (IT38) were not read first-hand here
context: Same preparation as BH1, with isolated NMDAR EPSC (AMPA and GABA-A blocked) measured in the same slices; recording Mg2+ and holding potential stated; the NAM is applied at concentrations chosen by measured percent current removed, not by the oocyte IC50 (the source slice used about 100 times the oocyte IC50 for a bath concentration); transfer from mouse hippocampal P17-P22 and oocytes to P13-P17 neocortex is unmeasured
competing_explanation: Total-gain or Mg2+-relief explanation (AB04, AB05): coincident curves; GluN2A-containing receptors carry the burst (H3); AMPAR-led drive (BH1); recording-state dependence (M14)
counter_evidence: Triheteromeric GluN2A/GluN2B receptors are inhibited only to 45 percent by radiprodil in oocytes, so a modest NAM effect is expected whatever the GluN2B share; radiprodil in vivo support is a GluN2B gain-of-function line; memantine 10 uM (text) or 30 uM (Fig 5 legend) did not inhibit the S810R EPSC; no WWOX subunit datum; the cortical GluN2 composition at P13-P17 in this knockout is not in any source read and is not a substitute for the measurement
weakening_result: The NAM curve coincides with the matched-current d-APV curve (no subunit specificity, in line with X2 of nmda_inv05); or the burst falls along the same curve as the AMPA-antagonist curve (M08) (general loss); or the NAM effect disappears at a higher Mg2+ (state)
discriminating_experiment: M01, M04 (d-APV titration with isolated EPSC), M05 (NAM at matched percent removed, d-APV at the end), M06 (TCN-201 at two measured co-agonist levels with glycine alone control), M14, M15; no within-slice washout reversal for radiprodil
status: IPOTESI; exploratory; the matched-current form already exists in the module as X2; independent audit: PARTLY (the delayed-response residual is largely a metric floor and is not evidence of incomplete block; M05 cannot split diheteromer from triheteromer share; radiprodil's slice Mg2+ is stated two ways in its source). What it now rests on: the absence of any isolated NMDAR current, subunit or Mg2+ datum for the preparation and the matched-current design
what_would_change_the_decision: A left-shifted NAM curve with a measured NAM-sensitive fraction makes a GluN2B-directed comparison the better question; coincident curves make total NMDAR reduction (and the Mg2+ and voltage of the bath) the question; a plateau below abolition with GluN2A-tool sensitivity at low but not high co-agonist moves the question to GluN2A-containing receptors. None of this can be taken from literature on cortical development or from other GRIN models. NEW MEASUREMENTS (not literature): within-slice paired design (each slice its own baseline, replacing the pooled-baseline unpaired comparisons of the source); recording Mg2+ and K+ as measured bath values; a receptor-agnostic release-reducing control; a floor control for the delayed-response metric.

chain: (1) DATO: carbenoxolone 100 uM cut burst frequency strongly and the effect did not recover on washout (text 87 percent mean-normalised; Table S1 median 0.84 to 0.03 per minute; Fig 3D bar about 0.1); the magnitude, the n (36/4 vs 13/6) and the amplitude statement are disputed between text, table and figure, so only the direction and the non-recovery are used. -> (2) DATO: the source itself says carbenoxolone may block NMDA receptors and blocks pannexin channels; brilliant blue FCF 10 uM did not lower burst frequency (median 0.84 to 0.78; n 73/6 vs 25/6) without any Panx1 engagement check. -> (3) DATO: in autaptic mouse hippocampal culture carbenoxolone 100 uM reduced AMPA EPSC to 63 percent and NMDA EPSC to 69 percent with a higher paired-pulse ratio (presynaptic), broadened spikes, lowered input resistance and reduced IPSCs (rapidly and fully reversible), while the EPSC reduction recovered incompletely; the AMPA-only glutamate-current test (95.7 percent) was run with NMDAR blocked, so direct NMDAR channel block was neither shown nor excluded. In rat CA1 slices carbenoxolone 100 uM (alone at P12, together with La3+ at P20) did not significantly change the reversed-uptake ischaemic glutamate current (P12 mean 22 percent lower, n = 6 against 14, P = 0.46, so an effect of the size found in culture is not excluded). -> (4) INFERENZA: the burst fall cannot be assigned to gap junctions; an effect on release and excitability is sufficient to explain it. -> (5) IPOTESI, benefit: the gap-junction half of the module's NMDAR-or-gap-junction wording stays withdrawn until a matched-effect control and a cleaner discrimination exist
pharmacological_action: Distinguish carbenoxolone's release, excitability and NMDAR effects from connexin or pannexin coupling by measuring EPSCs, spike width and coupling in the burst slices and by a matched-effect control
compound_or_probe: Carbenoxolone (19535488; 20940167; 23589583 Fig 6: blocks mouse Panx1 in oocytes, concentration not stated) as the compound whose off-target effects were read; brilliant blue FCF (23589583: Panx1 IC50 0.27 uM, plateau 75 to 85 percent in oocytes, no block of P2X7 or Cx46/Cx32E143 at 100 uM) with a Panx1 engagement measurement still to be made; mefloquine only if a primary mechanism and slice side-effect reading is obtained (abstract: Cx36 IC50 about 300 nM in N2A cells, 25 uM blocked interneuron coupling in neocortical slices, increased spontaneous synaptic activity); genetic ablation or dominant-negative approaches are the standard named by the Tovar authors
context: Neuron-specific Wwox knockout neocortical slices P13-P17 as in the source; culture data are mouse hippocampal micro-island neurons (P0-P1 origin, 6-15 DIV, room temperature), CA1 slices are rat P12/P20 at 33 C; transfer to the burst preparation is unmeasured
competing_explanation: Carbenoxolone acts through reduced release or excitability (H5); NMDAR block (H5, unresolved); Panx1 contributes (H6) but BB-FCF engagement is unverified; time-dependent run-down (M02); non-gap-junction K+ and Ca2+ effects of mefloquine
counter_evidence: The Tovar culture result points to a sizeable presynaptic release effect; Madry's CA1 result is low-powered against a 20-30 percent effect (22 percent lower, P = 0.46, n = 6 against 14) and reads a reversed-uptake ischaemic glutamate current, not evoked release, so it neither contradicts Tovar nor excludes an NMDAR block and carries little weight; both are kept, neither is slice data from this preparation
weakening_result: Carbenoxolone and a non-gap-junction manipulation matched to the same measured EPSC reduction produce the same burst fall (M10): H6 not supported and the coupling question not worth a connexin-selective arm; or brilliant blue FCF with demonstrated engagement lowers bursts (Panx1 supported)
discriminating_experiment: M01, M02, M09 (carbenoxolone with EPSC, AP width, Rin and a coupling readout), M10 (matched-effect control), M11 (BB-FCF with engagement), M13 only if a residual remains; paired within-slice design, M16 not required for the attribution but kept in BE5, because Tovar's carbenoxolone IPSC reduction could oppose a burst fall
status: IPOTESI; exploratory; premise not established; independent audit: PARTLY, close to a withdrawal of the gap-junction attribution. What survives: the direction-only reading of the carbenoxolone result, the off-target evidence from culture (with IPSC reversible and EPSC incomplete), the absence of any Panx1 engagement or connexin-selective test in the slice, and the measurement plan (EPSCs, spike width, coupling, matched controls); no datum in the sources read separates the gap-junction half from the off-target explanations (the carbenoxolone fall is not inconsistent with a coupling contribution; it is unattributable)
what_would_change_the_decision: A measured carbenoxolone effect on the slice's EPSCs large enough to account for the burst fall settles the attribution as non-gap-junction for this preparation; a residual burst fall beyond the matched control with coupling loss keeps the connexin question open. No literature on other preparations substitutes for the EPSC, spike and coupling measurements in these slices. NEW MEASUREMENTS (not literature): within-slice paired design; recording Mg2+ and K+ as measured values; a receptor-agnostic release-reducing control; two metrics for matched controls.
